classification.difficultyReason: Find intercepts and sketch lines, distinguishing lines through the origin and horizontal or vertical lines.

content.prompt: Sketch the graph of each equation, and mark the intercepts.

answer.worked:
When $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=2(0)+1\\y&=1\end{aligned}$$
When $y=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}2x+1&=0\\2x&=-1\\x&=-\frac12\end{aligned}$$
Draw the straight line through $(-\tfrac12,0)$ and $(0,1)$.

spec.description: Complete solution sketch with both intercepts labelled; no grid or ticks supplied in the source.

Draw the straight line through $(\tfrac32,0)$ and $(0,3)$.

Draw the straight line through $(3,0)$ and $(0,2)$.

Draw the straight line through $(4,0)$ and $(0,-3)$.

answer.worked: The $y$-coordinate is always $-4$, so draw a horizontal line through $(0,-4)$. This is the $y$-intercept. The line never meets the $x$-axis, so there is no $x$-intercept.
